$comment: The category/folder editor (app/category/edit.tsx) and the importance flow (app/category/importance.tsx).

category.note: Segmented control: this row is a category inside a folder.

folder.note: Segmented control: this row is a folder.

description.placeholder: What goes here, e.g. supermarkets, bakery, snacks
description.hint: The receipt scanner reads this to pick the category.

automatic.note: Icon/colour row subtitle: chosen from the name.

hint.message: A type says what a category is, whatever you call it — so a payment at a shop the app knows lands in the right one. Several categories can share a type. Changes are saved as you make them.
hint.note: Footer of Settings → Categories → Category types.

useAll.message: {count, plural, one {Use # suggestion} other {Use all # suggestions}}
useAll.note: Button: save every suggested type at once. count = how many categories have one.

undo.message: {count, plural, one {Undo — # category typed} other {Undo — # categories typed}}
undo.note: Button shown after Use all suggestions; puts the types back as they were.

needs.note: Section at the top of Category types: categories nobody has given a type yet.

choose.note: Under a category with no type and nothing to suggest.

fromHistory.note: type was guessed from the shops this category's payments went to; tap to keep or change.

suggestHere.note: Switch: may this category be offered because of where you are? Off by default for parking, taxi, bills.

also.note: Under a category type in the picker: the user's other categories that already have this type. names = comma-separated category names.

suggested.note: type is a category type's name, guessed from the category's name; saved on Save.

inheritedColour.message: Automatic uses {folder}’s colour, because the folder has one.

folderHint: A folder groups the list and is never filed into. New categories in it take its colour.

convert.notWithChildren: Not while there are categories inside it — move or convert those first
convert.rowSubtitle: {count, plural, one {Its # transaction keeps its history, gains the tag and moves where you choose} other {Its # transactions keep their history, gain the tag and move where you choose}}

where.message: {count, plural, one {Where does the # transaction go?} other {Where do the # transactions go?}}
where.note: Title of the sheet asking where a converted category's transactions move.

convert.parentSubtitle: The folder it is in — which becomes an ordinary category once this is its last one
convert.noneSubtitle: They keep the tag and nothing else

another.note: Used inside a sentence when the chosen category cannot be found.

title.note: Alert title; name is the category.

bodyMove.message: {count, plural, one {# transaction will get the tag “{tag}” and move to {home}.} other {# transactions will get the tag “{tag}” and move to {home}.}} The category is removed.
bodyMove.note: tag is the new tag's name, home the category they move to.

bodyNone.message: {count, plural, one {# transaction will get the tag “{tag}” and be left without a category.} other {# transactions will get the tag “{tag}” and be left without a category.}} The category is removed.
bodyNone.note: tag is the new tag's name.

archive.rowSubtitle: Keeps every transaction and every number; just stops being offered
archive.restoreSubtitle: Offered again everywhere it used to be
archive.keep: {count, plural, one {Its # transaction keeps it and still counts everywhere.} other {Its # transactions keep it and still count everywhere.}}
archive.inside: {count, plural, one {The # category inside goes with it.} other {The # categories inside go with it.}}
archive.offered: It stops being offered for anything new, including to the Shortcut automation, which will leave those payments in Pending for you to file.

delete.bodyChildren: {count, plural, one {Its # category becomes a top-level folder.} other {Its # categories become top-level folders.}} Transactions keep their data.
delete.body: Transactions keep their data but become uncategorized.

importance.title: Set what matters

header.note: Screen header on step 2 of marking what matters.

high.title: Which could you not live without?
high.hint: From what is left. If the money got tight, these are the ones you would still be paying: the roof, the food, the bills with consequences. Whatever you tick neither time stays in between.

header.note: Screen header on step 1 of marking what matters.

low.title: Which could you stop tomorrow?
low.hint: Nothing breaks if these stop — you would miss them, and that is all.

folderA11y.note: VoiceOver label of a folder row that ticks all its categories.

all.note: After a folder name: ticking it ticks all of its count categories.

importance.nothingLeft: Nothing left to ask about — the first question took everything.
importance.changes: {count, plural, one {# row changes} other {# rows change}}
importance.noChanges: Nothing changes: they already say this

folders.message: {count, plural, one {one folder answers for what is inside, so anything added to it later is already marked} other {# folders answer for what is inside, so anything added to them later is already marked}}

empty.title: No categories to mark
empty.hint: Importance is asked about expense categories that are not archived. Add some first.
